issue_context.title: AirNow can't change radius
issue_context.body:
### The problem

After the AirNow integration is added, there is no way to go back and edit the radius (without adding a new instance).

For other integrations there is a configure option that allows (some) changes to the initial parameters.

Some background: The default radius of 150 miles is too large for my area, Long Island, New York.  With the default radius, I get values for sensors that are fairly far away, across the water (Long Island Sound) in Connecticut. 

The problem winds up being that through the integration I get very high values that don't match the AirNow web page or the iOS mobile app.  So the integration appears as if it is generating bogus high values. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.6.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

AirNow

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/airnow/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

A related issue, https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/96018 at least for my area entering a radius during setup of less than 50 miles generated an "Unexpected Exception" during setup.  This appears to be from an empty response error (No data returned.)

The underlying cause of both of these issues is that the AirNow integration is giving me data that doesn't match my area, so it looks like the AirNow integration is giving bad data. What appears to be happening is that the AirNow API is returning data for a reporting area in another state.  That reporting area often has very different values. 

### Things that would help in this kind of situation:

1. Make the reporting area available as an attribute in the integration, so the data source can be checked within Home Assistant.
2. Enabled editing of the radius/distance without having to delete and re-add the integration.
3. Handle when the radius/distance is too small to return any observations more gracefully - see #96018
